newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up on blue-chip buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up on blue-chip buying.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up marginally on Friday on institutional buying in blue-chips, but other stocks largely languished pending the release of the bulk of the 1996 results, brokers said.
Of 43 B share companies, less than 10 have so far issued annual results with the April 30 deadline approaching.
The B index edged up 0.218 points or 0.3 percent to 73.320 on volume of 13.2 million shares worth $8.1 million compared with $12.1 million on Thursday.
Some overseas funds were seen flowing into the market as a result of the recent strong performance by Chinese stocks listed in Hong Kong, brokers said.
"We can see some overseas investors buying blue-chips," said one broker. "But trading was still sluggish today with no buyers for most shares."
"The market will rise further if more overseas capital flows into the market," another broker said.
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded, with 17 up, nine flat and 16 down.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the star on institutional buying, jumping $0.044 or 5.83 percent to $0.798 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Another blue-chip, portable phone maker Eastern Communications, traded the most on overseas buying, ending up $0.032 or 3.14 percent at $1.050 on volume of 1.5 million shares.
The Shanghai A share index ended down on investor jitters over the possibility of a government crackdown on excessive speculation in the market, brokers said.
The index dipped 3.709 points or 0.28 percent to 1,340.593 on volume of 875.6 million shares worth 11.0 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index fell 23.500 points or 0.66 percent to 3,512.598 points.
Chongqing Department Store was the biggest loser on institutional selling, down 1.37 yuan or 6.77 percent to 18.85 yuan on volume of 2.9 million shares.
